Task.Prompt: From a labelled rigid motion match corresponding sides and angles and write a complete theorem proof. Draw a nondegenerate triangle, rotate 180 degrees about a longest-side midpoint, construct the resulting quadrilateral and justify it is a parallelogram.

Criteria.Criterion: correctly maps corresponding labelled vertices, sides and angles from the specified rigid transformation
gives a logically noncircular theorem proof that the same rigid motion maps all corresponding parts and preserves measures
shows accurate nondegenerate triangle, side midpoint and image after 180-degree rotation, with matching opposite rays
proves the formed quadrilateral is a parallelogram from shared-midpoint diagonals or justified parallel sides, not visual appearance

Items.SourceFocus: reflection rectangle ABCD to DCBA: reason AB congruent DC
Items.ExpectedTeacherEvidence: D: corresponding parts of congruent figures are congruent, supported by the rigid map; reverse statement C is not the theorem

Items.SourceFocus: isosceles triangle FEH reflected over HF to FGH
Items.ExpectedTeacherEvidence: FE=HE, FE=FG, HE=HG; EFGH four equal sides; FH angle bisector at F and H; angle FEH congruent FGH. On provided valid figure B,C,E; justify why A,D are not forced.

Items.SourceFocus: reflect right triangle ABC across line BC
Items.ExpectedTeacherEvidence: C is on mirror so CA equals CA prime; ACA prime is at least isosceles. Do not deduce an equilateral label without extra data.

Items.SourceFocus: two translated images of triangle ABC, FAD and DCE
Items.ExpectedTeacherEvidence: evaluate original diagram-dependent claim options by explicit point maps, equal angle and parallel-vector reasoning
use corresponding angles and a valid straight-line/parallel argument, not diagram appearance

Items.SourceFocus: choose rigid image among six drawn quadrilaterals
Items.ExpectedTeacherEvidence: teacher checks the actual labelled image and a complete reflection/rotation/translation description
